summary: The exported fetch-native MCP handler accepts requests without enforcing Host or Origin validation, making a directly mounted local handler plausibly reachable through DNS rebinding.
evidence: createMcpHandler returns fetchFace, which forwards the caller-controlled Request directly to handle without consulting hostHeaderValidationResponse or originValidationResponse. The package documentation at lines 1167-1183 explicitly says the entry is deliberately validation-free and requires consumers to add those checks in front, so a consumer following the direct handler.fetch mounting API without the optional wrapper has no in-handler DNS-rebinding boundary.
context: The package documents a secure wrapper and the helpers are available, so validation should determine whether any production consumer exposes this handler without upstream Host/Origin enforcement and whether dependency findings are reportable under the repository policy.

summary: The MCP HTTP handler buffers and parses an entire unauthenticated POST body without an in-handler size limit, allowing plausible memory and CPU exhaustion.
evidence: fetchFace passes the Request to handle, which calls classifyEntryRequest. For POST requests without a pre-parsed body, classifyEntryRequest clones the request and executes await request.text() at line 1059 before JSON.parse at line 1064. No Content-Length check, byte counter, stream cap, or other body-size bound appears on this path.
context: Exploitability depends on how consumers expose the handler and on any request-size limit imposed by their runtime or reverse proxy; the exported fetch handler itself does not enforce one.

summary: Octokit RequestError preserves portions of access_token and client_secret query values for common characters and casing variants, so logging the error can disclose credentials.
evidence: RequestError copies the request, then redacts URL secrets with the case-sensitive patterns /client_secret=\w+/ and /access_token=\w+/. Values containing URL-encoded or punctuation characters are only partially replaced (for example, access_token=abc%2Fdef becomes access_token=[REDACTED]%2Fdef and client_secret=abc-def becomes client_secret=[REDACTED]-def), while uppercase parameter names are unchanged. The resulting URL remains on the public error.request object; fetch-wrapper constructs and throws this error with requestOptions.
context: Validation should confirm which query parameter forms are supported or reachable through normal Octokit request construction and whether downstream logging/serialization includes error.request; the standalone request URL API accepts arbitrary URLs.
